problem: Pretrained diffusion navigation policies (e.g. NavDP) are bounded by offline imitation data coverage, so under distribution shift they produce trajectories with insufficient obstacle clearance and collisions. Existing RL fine-tuning for diffusion policies (DPPO) needs a critic trained from scratch plus frozen and trainable actor copies, which is memory-heavy and unstable.
motivation: Safe deployment of learned navigation foundation models needs online adaptation that instills safety margins without extra expert demonstrations. Diffusion sampling naturally produces multiple trajectory candidates per observation, which fits group-relative advantage estimation and removes the need for a value network.
key_idea: Fine-tune a pretrained diffusion navigation policy (NavDP) with critic-free GRPO over groups of 16 sampled trajectories scored by an analytic occupancy-grid reward, updating only the top decoder layers and action head.
insight: Freezing most of the model is essential: fine-tuning the full model gives no gain over NavDP (0.520 SR) and a much higher variance (±0.066), while the last 5 layers give 0.587 and the last 2 layers 0.573. Restricting the importance ratio to the last K=7 denoising steps beats K=10 (0.532), and removing clipping (0.553) or advantage normalization (0.565) hurts. GRPO also beats actor-critic DPPO (0.527 SR), suggesting group-relative comparison is more effective than a from-scratch critic.
method: Trajectory-level policy: the diffusion policy is treated as a distribution over H=24 waypoint trajectories, and the log-likelihood is the sum of Gaussian reverse-step transitions along the denoising chain.

Analytic trajectory reward: G=16 candidates per observation are scored in memory, without execution, on a local 2D occupancy grid built from depth and its inflated version. Terms: success +10, progress +3, collision -5, inflated collision -1, distance -0.1, smoothness -0.1, zig-zag -0.05.

GRPO objective: advantages are group-normalized (R-mean)/(std+eps), with a PPO-style clipped surrogate; the importance ratio is computed from cached denoising-chain noise predictions of the old policy, and KL beta=0.

Selective fine-tuning: the perception encoders (two DepthAnythingV2-S) and first 11 of 16 DiT layers are frozen; only layers 11-15 and the action head are trained (11.83M of 173.59M params); gradients use only the last K=7 denoising steps.

Offline buffered training: 8 iterations, each collecting 130 episodes over a rolling window of 4 scenes into a disk replay buffer (capacity 128); 2 epochs, batch 64, lr 1e-5; the best checkpoint is chosen by windowed average reward.
Real deployment: the planner runs at ~2 Hz on a Jetson Orin and an MPC tracker at 25 Hz, so waypoints transfer across embodiments (wheeled Dingo to Unitree Go2).

setting.backbone: NavDP diffusion policy (DepthAnythingV2-S encoders + 16-layer DiT decoder), RL fine-tuned with GRPO
setting.training_data: NavDP pretrained on large-scale simulation data; RL fine-tuning by online interaction in 4-scene rolling windows from InternScenes-Home scenes 11-19 (8 iterations x 130 episodes), no expert demonstrations
setting.observation: RGB-D history of 8 frames plus relative goal vector (front-facing camera)
setting.action_space: predicted 24 waypoints in the local frame, tracked by an MPC controller
setting.simulator: Isaac Sim 4.2 / Isaac Lab 1.2 (InternScenes-Home); zero-shot Habitat qualitative
setting.privileged: none at test time (privileged depth-derived occupancy is used only for the training reward)

numbers.eval_set_note: 11 held-out scenes (Home 0-10), 101 tasks each, 1,111 episodes, mean of 3 seeds; success radius 1.5 m
numbers.extra: RL fine-tuned in Isaac Sim on Home 11-19; no expert data
OOD geometric primitives, no residential furniture
numbers.evidence: OOD Geometric Generalization: 90.1% SR and 0.861 SPL vs 88.1% and 0.851 for baseline

numbers.eval_set_note: 20 trials (10 narrow corridor, 10 cluttered office), any collision counts as failure
numbers.extra: sim-to-real, cross-embodiment (Dingo to Go2), no real-world training

numbers_note: SR in the InternScenes-Home rows is printed as 0.587 in Table 1 and 58.7% in the text; it is given here as 58.7 and SPL is kept as printed. The Table 1 SPL of DD-PPO (0.362) is odd but is a baseline.
results: On unseen InternScenes-Home scenes, SR rises from 52.0 (NavDP) to 58.7 and SPL from 0.49 to 0.537, beating DPPO (52.7 / 0.488), ViPlanner (40.2) and iPlanner (36.2). Gains also hold on seen scenes (60.1 to 68.7), on the OOD Hard scenes (88.1 to 90.1) and on a real Go2 (50% to 70%).
limitations: Gains are moderate and evaluated only in Isaac Sim InternScenes-Home; the real-world test is small (20 trials) and the Habitat transfer is qualitative only.
Purely reactive local planner without global routing for long-horizon navigation, with weak embodiment awareness in tight spaces such as under tables; ~500 ms inference latency per step.
Reward requires depth-derived occupancy and the method depends on the NavDP base; hyperparameters (N=5 layers, K=7) are tuned empirically.
